issues.body: The new text says the requirement to put the policy in a shared module "so the two cannot diverge" was already honored, but immediately states that this federated module was deliberately not rewired. Inspection of f85d0180 confirms sparq-engine imports sparq_replan_policy::ReplanPolicy while sparq-fedplan retains its own ReplanPolicy and trigger/hysteresis implementation. Merely creating a shared crate for one consumer does not prevent the two paths from drifting, so this is an inaccurate architectural claim in the durable module documentation.
issues.fix_hint: State precisely that the prior branch extracted a candidate shared policy and wired only the local evaluator to it, while the federated evaluator intentionally remained unchanged; therefore convergence onto one implementation was not completed and drift prevention was not achieved. Preserve the valid point that rewiring fedplan should not be done as a standalone change without a main-branch local consumer.
issues.title: Shared-policy claim contradicts the implementation

verdict.summary: The historical commit and the scoped research record support most of the new prior-art note, including the unmerged feature, non-canonical negative benchmark, and missing pruning-arm measurement. However, the note materially overstates the shared-policy result: the cited branch only makes the local evaluator consume sparq-replan-policy and explicitly leaves sparq-fedplan on its independent in-file policy. Therefore the two implementations can still diverge, contrary to the claim that the sharing requirement was already honored.
